cards.explanation: The answer is He spares them. Joel 2:18 says, “Then the LORD became jealous for His land, and He spared His people.” After all that locust trouble, that's a sentence worth reading twice, friends. I'd read it a third time just to hear it.

The answer is grain, new wine and oil. God says, “Behold, I will send you grain, new wine, and oil, and by them you will be satisfied.” Three things, and the verse says they'll bring satisfaction. If a batch of mine could promise that, friends, I'd frame the recipe.

The answer is True. God says, “I will never again make you a reproach among the nations.” A reproach is something people look down on. Here God says He will not make His people that again, and I'd say that's one of the best promises in the whole passage, friends.
The answer is Western. Joel 2:20 says the front ranks go “…into the Eastern Sea, and its rear guard into the Western Sea.” The front ranks go to one sea and the rear guard goes to the other, friends.

The answer is because the LORD has done great things. Joel 2:21 says, “Do not be afraid, O land; rejoice and be glad, for the LORD has done great things.” The reason for the gladness is what He has done, friends. I think that's a lot easier to rejoice over than a to-do list.

The answer is green. Joel 2:22 says, “…for the open pastures have turned green…” Green pastures are a good reason for the beasts of the field to stop being afraid. Even a hungry animal can read that sign, friends.

The answer is False. Joel 2:22 says, “…the fig tree and vine yield their best.” So they give their best, they don't hold it back, friends. The trees bear their fruit too, and I'd say that's a happy orchard.

The answer is autumn and spring rains. Joel 2:23 says, “He sends you showers, both autumn and spring rains, as before.” Both rains, and as before, friends. A baker knows how much good timing matters, and I'd say rain on time is a gift.

The first blank is full, and the second is overflow. Joel 2:24 says, “The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.” A threshing floor is where grain gets separated from the stalks, so picture it crowded with grain, friends. Overflow means more than enough, spilling over the edges. I know a mixing bowl that does this sometimes, and I do not enjoy cleaning that up.

The answer is that He will repay His people for them. God says, “I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts…” He looks at the years that were lost and says repay, friends. That's a promise to take in slowly.

The answer is, “My great army that I sent.” After the four kinds of locusts, God says, “…My great army that I sent against you.” He calls them His army, and He says He sent them, friends. I'd read that line slowly, because it says a lot in a few words.

The answer is praise. Joel 2:26 says, “You will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has worked wonders for you.” With plenty to eat, praise follows, friends. I'd say a full table can make a person thankful.

The answer is that God is present in Israel. In Joel 2:27 God says, “Then you will know that I am present in Israel and that I am the LORD your God, and there is no other.” After everything He does, this is what they'll know, friends. I think that's better than any harvest.

The answer is True. In Joel 2:27 God says, “…I am the LORD your God, and there is no other.” He says it plainly, in His own words, friends. After the locusts and the hard years, that is a firm place to stand.
